models_evaluated: Llama family and other Claude models (M2-M5)

links.outcome: Ambient scribe ICU note omissions, commissions (hallucinations), partial errors against transcript-derived elements
links.effect: Omission errors mean 15.5%, partial 7.2%, commission 2.6% combined; M1 accuracy 69% vs M6 80% (P=.04); omission 21.6% vs 9.32%.
links.quote: Overall, errors of omission were most common (mean 15.5%, SEM 2.7%), followed by partial errors (mean 7.2%, SEM 0.92%) and then errors of commission (mean 2.6%, SEM 0.7%).

links.outcome: Local assessment of scribe documentation accuracy, quality (PDQI-9), and error severity
links.effect: Accuracy 69% vs 80%; PDQI-9 35.8 vs 38.3 (P=.06); most errors no to low harm potential; time savings and well-being not measured.
links.quote: Finally, in terms of overall readability and usefulness, M6 was better than M1 based on PDQI-9 scores, but the difference was not statistically significant (M1=35.8, SEM 0.78 vs M6=38.3, SEM 0.53; P =.06).

links.outcome: Note accuracy after model upgrade and prompt updates
links.effect: Prompt iterations improved M1 accuracy from 57.25% (V1) to 69.15% (V4); upgraded M6 reached 80.3% vs 69.12% (P=.04), with more commission errors (3.92% vs 1.30%).
links.quote: In comparison, model M6, a direct upgrade of model 1 ( Multimedia Appendix 1 for model description), performed better across all 5 cases, achieving an overall accuracy of 80.3% (95% CI 75.2%‐85.5%; P =.04).

links.outcome: Variability in output quality across LLMs using the same prompt
links.effect: Same prompt gave widely varying accuracy across models in phase 1 (e.g., M2 33.5% vs M1 57-74%); M4 declined after prompt updates.
links.quote: M4 initially performed well but showed inconsistent results and a decline in performance after updates.

links.outcome: Omitted or unsupported content in AI notes that clinicians would need to catch
links.effect: Errors of omission, commission and partial errors were present in AI notes; authors note manual review is the current safeguard and may cause automation complacency.
links.quote: This is especially important, given that the current safeguard against errors in AI scribe notes is manual review by clinicians, which adds an additional burden on clinicians and could lead to automation complacency and/or bias [ 37-42 ].

links.outcome: Potential for automation complacency with manual review of scribe notes
links.effect: Authors state manual review adds burden and could lead to automation complacency; not measured directly.
links.quote: This is especially important, given that the current safeguard against errors in AI scribe notes is manual review by clinicians, which adds an additional burden on clinicians and could lead to automation complacency and/or bias [ 37-42 ].

links.effect: For M1, correct rose from 57.25% (V1) to 73.80% (V3) and 69.15% (V4); omission fell from 31.60% to 16.85% (V3).
links.quote: Iterative improvements to the prompt increased accuracy and reduced errors during phase 1.

links.effect: Phase 1 correct ranged 33.50% (M2 V1) to 73.80% (M1 V3); phase 2 M6 accuracy was 80.3% versus M1 69.12% (P=.04).
links.quote: In comparison, model M6, a direct upgrade of model 1 ( Multimedia Appendix 1 for model description), performed better across all 5 cases, achieving an overall accuracy of 80.3% (95% CI 75.2%‐85.5%; P =.04).

links.effect: M6 improved accuracy (80.3% vs M1 69.12%, P=.04) and omissions (9.32% vs 21.60%, adjusted P=.03), but commissions were higher (3.92% vs 1.30%).
links.quote: Comparison of error subtypes between the 2 models showed that only omission errors (21.60% vs 9.32%; adjusted P value =.03) were statistically significantly different between M1 and M6.

links.effect: Errors occurred despite M1/M6 accuracies of 69.12%/80.32%; omissions averaged 15.5%, partial errors 7.2%, and commissions 2.6%.
links.quote: Overall, errors of omission were most common (mean 15.5%, SEM 2.7%), followed by partial errors (mean 7.2%, SEM 0.92%) and then errors of commission (mean 2.6%, SEM 0.7%).

links.effect: Combined phase-2 errors: omissions 15.5%, partial 7.2%, commissions 2.6%; examples included plan omissions and unsupported transfusion/code-status content.
links.quote: Overall, errors of omission were most common ( Figure 5 ) with an average of 15.5 (SEM 2.7%, 95% CI 9.4%‐21.6%), followed by partial errors at 7.2 (SEM 0.92%, 95% CI 5.1%‐9.3%), with errors of commission being the least common at 2.6 (SEM 0.7%, 95% CI 1.1%‐4.1%).
